role: One 32-bit pad-configuration register per physical pin (26 pins on ESP32-C3: GPIO0-21 plus 4 pins with no GPIO number). Selects which of up to 6 signals drives the pad (function 1 is almost always 'plain GPIO', routed onward through the GPIO matrix), plus pull-up/down, drive strength, input-enable and sleep-mode overrides. Genuinely pure data -- every field is RMW storage with no side effect on read and no poll target found anywhere in the boot path. esp-soc's chip file currently lists IO_MUX as "model": "stub" with the note 'reads-as-written serves the RMW config patterns' -- this file is that promotion to a cited regmap, one register template plus the per-pin offset table.
verified: 2026-08-24 field template (SLP_*, FUN_*, MCU_SEL, FILTER_EN) and the GPIO2 register offset (0x0c) and its function-select values quoted directly from the header at the pinned tag. The remaining 25 pins' offsets follow the same header's IO_MUX_GPIOn_REG table (io_mux_reg.h:96-114+) and were not individually re-quoted here -- draft the full 26-entry offset table mechanically from that macro block rather than retyping it by hand.

fields.name: SLP_OE
fields.why: Output-enable override while the RTC domain is in sleep; not exercised before app_main()

fields.name: SLP_SEL
fields.why: Marks this pin as a sleep wakeup source

fields.name: FUN_PD
fields.why: Pulldown enable in the pin's normal (non-sleep) function

fields.name: FUN_PU
fields.why: Pullup enable; Arduino's INPUT_PULLUP sets this via gpio_pullup_en()

fields.name: FUN_IE
fields.why: Input-enable. Must be set for a pin used as UART RX or as a digitalRead() input, or the pad never drives its input buffer and GPIO_IN always reads 0 for that pin regardless of the external signal

fields.name: FUN_DRV
fields.why: Output drive strength (5/10/20/40 mA); cosmetic for a simulator, stored so readback matches

fields.name: MCU_SEL
fields.why: Function select, 0-5 (this pin's GPIO2 example: 0=GPIO2_0/analog default, 1=GPIO2 digital GPIO, 2=FSPIQ). This is the field IO_MUX contributes to the 'any pin to (almost) any signal' story from docs/architectures.md 4.3 item 7: MCU_SEL must equal the pin's own 'route through GPIO matrix' function value (1 on every C3 pin checked) before the GPIO-matrix FUNCn_OUT_SEL_CFG/FUNCn_IN_SEL_CFG registers (see gpio-contract.json) have any effect at all. Get MCU_SEL wrong and the matrix routing is set up correctly in software but the pad itself is still listening to some other peripheral's dedicated function -- a silent miswire, not a hang

fields.name: FILTER_EN
fields.why: Glitch filter on the input path; not exercised before app_main()

function_values.name: FUNC_GPIO2_GPIO2
function_values.why: the value gpio_ll / IDF's GPIO driver writes to route this pad through the GPIO matrix

per_pin_offset_note: IO_MUX_GPIOn_REG for n=0..21 plus 4 non-GPIO pins are #define aliases to PERIPHS_IO_MUX_<padname>_U macros at io_mux_reg.h:96-114 and following; several pin names are the pad's other bonded function (e.g. IO_MUX_GPIO4_REG -> PERIPHS_IO_MUX_MTMS_U, IO_MUX_GPIO12_REG -> PERIPHS_IO_MUX_SPIHD_U) because those pads are shared with JTAG or the in-package SPI flash on some C3 modules. GPIO12-17 in particular are frequently NOT available on modules with in-package flash -- the chip file's pin table (not yet written by anyone this session) should flag that per board, not assume all 22 GPIOs are free.
